segments.heading: Overview
segments.text: In this tutorial, we will install Arbiter using the standard workflow: stage it locally with Reploy, configure and test it, then install it as a permanent Docker service on the system.

guide.success_hint: The installer should report that Reploy is ready.
You should enter the staging directory and see the selected runtime bundle.

segments.heading: Bootstrap Docker Staging Directory
segments.text: Use Reploy to create the staging directory. Then enter it; the rest of the setup runs from inside that staged deployment.

guide.success_hint: You should still be inside reploy-staging and see the selected bundle roots.

segments.heading: Select Mail Bundle
segments.text: Arbiter has a pluggable architecture. For this demo, we add the IMAP and SMTP plugins. First, list the available bundle options. Then add the mail plugins. Now build the bundle. Reploy builds a local bundle from the selected dependencies, and that bundle becomes part of the staged app. Installation will use the tested artifact instead of resolving packages again later. Reploy rebuilds the bundle automatically when dependencies change; running the build here pays that cost now instead of during the next app command.

commands: reploy app config activate --plugin smtp --account mail-demo
reploy app bootstrap --plugin imap --account mail-demo --variant default-open
reploy app config activate --plugin imap --account mail-demo
guide.success_hint: The normal and live config checks should both pass.

segments.heading: Bootstrap Arbiter Config
segments.text: In this section, we will configure Arbiter to use the local test SMTP and IMAP servers. We will create one account named mail-demo in each plugin, with broad access so the demo can focus on installation and smoke testing, not on every policy option exposed by the mail plugins. Start by creating the server config. Take a quick look at arbiter-server.yaml. This file is the Hydra entry point: it selects the server schema, plugin list, and the env file used at startup. Next, bootstrap the SMTP account and policy. SMTP's generated policy is broad by default: empty recipient allow and block lists mean Arbiter is not restricting recipients yet. The account file points at the SMTP host and credentials. The policy keeps rate limits visible, leaves recipient restrictions open, and warns instead of failing if the matching IMAP Sent copy cannot be written. For the recording, we edit these files to use the local test SMTP server. Activate the SMTP account in the composed config. Then bootstrap the Arbiter env file. Open .arbiter.env and enter the SMTP username and password from the test mail lab. To test mail sending end to end, add the matching IMAP account too. The IMAP bootstrap uses the default-open variant, which starts with broad folder access and lets you add deny rules later. Inspect the generated IMAP account. The IMAP policy allows read and search broadly, and this demo edits it to allow writes as well. Edit the IMAP files for the local test server. Activate the IMAP account. Re-run env bootstrap; it is incremental, so it adds the new IMAP variables without throwing away the SMTP values. Open .arbiter.env again and add the IMAP username and password. Now run a normal config check. It validates the composed YAML and schemas. Finally, run a live config check; this also logs into the test IMAP and SMTP servers.
